# #409 — [Epic] PROV: port the Claude lifecycle adapter to Python as a uv workspace package

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-07-25T23:34:17Z
Updated: 2026-07-25T23:38:03Z

---

## The finding

The Claude/Claudex lifecycle adapter is **7,513 lines of TypeScript whose main job is `spawnSync` into the Python CLI**. It is a shell around `openbrain-memory`, and the shell is a net negative today: it has produced two silent-failure incidents, and it duplicates domain vocabulary that has already drifted.

Measured 2026-07-25:

| Symptom | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Silent capture drop | `event_type: "finding"` is not in the adapter's `EVENT_TYPES`. `buildPackageRequest` returns `null`, `runProvider` returns `""`, exit 0. No receipt, no row, no error. Found only by checking psql. |
| Enum already drifted | `openbrain_memory/agent.py` declares **9** event types; the TS adapter declares **8** — missing `question`. Two hand-maintained copies of one vocabulary. |
| Undifferentiated failure | 11 distinct `return null` paths in `buildPackageRequest` collapse into 5 identical silent-return sites. Oversized input, malformed JSON, bad correlation id, unknown event type and empty content are indistinguishable to the caller. |
| Prior incident, same class | `uv` began colorizing `uv tool dir`; `isAbsolute()` saw `\033[36m/Users/...` and returned false. That parse failure **disabled Open Brain session-start recall entirely** and reported it as "lane memory unavailable" — a local string-parsing bug reported as a remote availability problem. |
| Install layout | `~/.local/share/openbrain-memory/` holds a `.venv`, a private `uv-cache`, a hand-built wheelhouse (7 `.whl`), and `adapters/versions/sha256-*/` — **8 versions in 8 days, nothing prunes them**. `~/.claude/settings.json` hardcodes **13 absolute paths** into one hash. |
| Already over the file limit | `ob-memory-provider.ts` is 1,954 lines and `context-budget-gate.ts` is 1,066. `CODING_STANDARDS.md` sets a 750-line hard limit, 600-line split review. |

`CODING_STANDARDS.md` already names the rule the silent drop violates:

> *"If a failure category is already computed (e.g. `errorCategory`), the operator must see it: exporting it to telemetry only is not an error message."*

`runProvider` computes `result.errorCategory`, emits it to Langfuse, and returns `""` to the caller.

## Decision

**Port the adapter to Python. One source of truth in dev.** TypeScript is not maintained alongside it; if a TS artifact is ever needed it is generated on merge, not hand-kept current.

Hooks do not require TypeScript — `~/.claude/settings.json` entries are `"type": "command"`, arbitrary shell. `bun run <hash-path>/claude-hook.ts` becomes a console script. No TS consumer imports these modules as a library; the only importers (`context-budget-gate.ts` → `ob-memory-provider.ts` → `receipt-state.ts`) are inside the set being ported.

**The bugs are fixed by being written correctly in Python, not fixed in TS first.** A TS fix would be deleted by the port. Correct behavior is the acceptance criteria of each sub-issue, not separate work.

## Home and shape

`open-brain/python/` becomes a **uv workspace**, following the proven `fleet-bus` pattern (root `pyproject.toml` with `[tool.uv.workspace]`, sibling packages under it, each with its own `pyproject.toml` + hatchling + ruff/mypy/pytest config, `src/<pkg>/` layout, **flat modules — no domain subfolders**).

```
open-brain/python/
  pyproject.toml            # NEW workspace root
  openbrain-memory/         # existing, becomes a member, otherwise unchanged
  openbrain-provider/       # NEW
    src/openbrain_provider/ # flat modules, ~100-250 lines each
    tests/
```

Small files that do one thing: one place to change when something breaks. Console scripts (`ob-memory-provider`, `ob-claude-hook`, `ob-context-budget-gate`, `ob-guard`) replace the 13 hardcoded `sha256-` paths.

## Standards this must satisfy

Not aspirations — existing rules in `_DOCS/CODING_STANDARDS.md`, `king-capital/docs/coding-standards.md`, and `rtech-hermes/docs/coding-standards.md`:

- Python ≥3.13, `uv` only, `uv.lock` committed, frozen installs in CI.
- Gates: `ruff format` + `ruff check` (incl. pydocstyle `D` google convention), `mypy` strict, `pytest`. **Pre-push and CI command-identical over the same paths.**
- Loguru only, never `print()`; five log points; `serialize=True`, `enqueue=True`, `contextualize()`; envelope imported from `rtech-standards`, never copied from a document.
- `try/except/finally` around external calls, file ops, hook invocations. No bare `except:`. **Every intentional fail-open is a documented decision in the code stating why.**
- `config.py` = frozen dataclasses with `__post_init__` validation; `logger.py` = setup only, no business logic; module-level `UPPER_CASE` constants, no inline magic.
- Testing is functional I/O. Coverage percentages are explicitly not acceptance criteria.
- 750-line hard limit, split at ~600.
